independent.summary: The new comment on the `form.dataset.native` guard says it is "Set below, when the ladder has run out", but nothing in the repo ever sets `data-native` (grep over src/, functions/, server/, test/ finds only this read). The guard is dead code and the comment states something untrue about the ladder, so a future reader will assume a native-post fallback exists that does not.

triageGrades.reason: The diff only rewrites client-side inline scripts and one test regex; no authentication, session or access-control code is involved.
No credentials, tokens or env bindings appear or change; the only stored value is the light/dark theme key.
No price or `money()` usage is touched — the SpeedProof numbers are kilobytes and milliseconds, and the median still comes from `benchmarks.medianPageKb` (2311).
No migrations, deletions or data-destroying operations; `localStorage.removeItem('theme')` is pre-existing theme behavior, unchanged.

The only network call is the pre-existing same-origin `fetch('/api/contact')`, whose status ladder (ok/redirected → sent=1, non-404/405 → sent=0, 404/405 → mailto) is preserved exactly; no third-party API is involved.
No CI, deploy config, migration or go-live file changes; `astro.config.mjs` and `public/_headers` are untouched.

summary: Reporting no defects was close to right — the rewrite is behavior-preserving (the cached branch, the 404/405 ladder and the 2311 KB median all come out identical, and the built pages still inline the now-bundled modules so the inline-script and no-external-bundle budgets hold) — but the review was shallow: it offered no evidence it checked equivalence or the built output, and it missed the newly added comment that misdescribes the dead `data-native` guard.
